g.text: UDP hole punching: both sides send first, so both NATs open a door
Each NAT only admits replies to something its own side sent out.
3 pong / data: both NATs now have a door - direct path
In Tailscale the "ping/pong" are small "disco" messages sent to every candidate endpoint, and a CallMeMaybe message (relayed via DERP) makes the peer start probing too.
WireGuard traffic switches to the first path that answers.
